analysis:
The PR changes provider memory reclamation and load admission and touches no authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator-contract code.

ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift (lines 70-71) only has a comment update, so there is no behavior change.

ProviderLoop+MemoryProtection.swift (head line 60) adds CBv2RetainedKVSegments.requestRelease() to the memory-pressure clearCache closure. It sits after the native MiMo reclamation guards, so the existing safety checks are preserved. The call only signals engines to drop retained free KV segments. This releases memory and cannot expose prompt data. It is arguably positive for T-028, since it reduces residual KV data in memory. The implementation of CBv2RetainedKVSegments is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that it zeroes or frees segments safely.

ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (patch ~1306-1412 and ~1531):
- reclaimableMemoryBytes now includes CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes in the reclaimable figure.
- releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad is new. It awaits GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments(), then clears the MLX cache via clearCacheAfterConfirmedNativeOwnership(), which keeps the native ownership confirmation.
- evictUntilAvailable gains a one-time pool drop before eviction. It is gated on busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory().
- Both existing clearCache sites now call the new helper.

This affects availability only. The risks are (a) reclaimable memory being over-counted if retained segments are not actually released, which would admit a load that then OOMs (T-016/T-029 availability class), and (b) the wait in releaseRetainedKVSegments being unbounded while the load gate is held. The patch comment says it waits briefly, but the implementation is outside the supplied evidence. Neither is a demonstrated regression.

No interaction with the T-041 prefix cache, the SSD tier, cacheSalt or the at-rest artifacts is visible. The prefix-cache behavior is unchanged.

Remaining integration questions: the bounded timeout of GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments, and whether the retained KV segments hold any cross-request plaintext that is reused (a T-028 concern). The ModelLoading patch excerpt was truncated, so the eviction loop edits are only partially visible.
